blocks.content: Not less than one-third of the total number of seats reserved for women shall be allotted by rotation to different constituencies in a Panchayat.

rows: In proportion to their population in the Panchayat area
Not less than one-third (33%) of total seats and chairperson posts
As determined at the discretion of the State Legislature

items: Article 243D specifically governs reservation of seats and offices of Chairpersons in Panchayati Raj Institutions.
Women reservation in Panchayats is a mandatory provision (minimum 33%), whereas reservation for Backward Classes (OBCs) is an optional/voluntary provision for states.
The 83rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 exempted Arunachal Pradesh from SC reservations in Panchayats due to the absence of SC population in the state.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 243D provides for mandatory reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in every Panchayat in proportion to their population.
Not less than one-third of the total number of seats are mandatorily reserved for women, including seats reserved for SC and ST women.
Offices of Chairpersons at the village, intermediate, and district levels are also reserved for SCs, STs, and women in a manner determined by the State Legislature.
Reservation for Backward Classes (OBCs) in Panchayats is voluntary and left entirely to the discretion of the respective State Legislatures.
The 83rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 2000 exempted Arunachal Pradesh from reserving seats for SCs, as the state has no SC population.
